{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2017–18 |team=Houston Cougars |image=Houston Cougars primary logo.svg |image_size=150 |short_conf=AAC |CoachRank= 22 |APRank= 21 |record=27–8 |conf_record=14–4 |head_coach=[[Kelvin Sampson]] |hc_year=4th |asst_coach1=[[Alvin Brooks (basketball, born 1959)|Alvin Brooks]] |asst_coach2=[[Kellen Sampson]] |asst_coach3=[[Quannas White]] |stadium=[[Health and Physical Education Arena|H&PE Arena]] (temporary arena) |champion= |bowl= [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = Second Round }} {{2017–18 American Athletic Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2017–18 Houston Cougars men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Houston]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Cougars were led by fourth-year head coach [[Kelvin Sampson]] as members of the [[American Athletic Conference]]. Due to renovations to the Cougars home arena, [[Hofheinz Pavilion]], they played their home games at the [[Health and Physical Education Arena|H&PE Arena]] on the campus of [[Texas Southern University]]. The Cougars ended the season with a record of 27–8. They tied for second place in regular-season conference play with a record of 14–4. As the No. 3 seed in the [[2018 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]], Houston advanced to the final game, losing 56–55 to the [[2017–18 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati Bearcats]]. The Cougars earned a No. 6 seed in the West Regional of the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], where they advanced to the second round before falling to the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan Wolverines]] by a score of 64–63. ==Previous season== The [[2016–17 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Cougars]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 21–11, 12–6 in [[2016–17 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]] to finish in third place. They lost to [[2016–17 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2017 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-uconn-men-game-aac-houston-0311-20170310-story.html|title=Jalen Adams Helps UConn Stun Houston In AAC Quarterfinals|last=AMORE|first=DOM|work=courant.com|access-date=2017-07-24|language=en-US}} They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] as a No. 2 seed and lost in the first round to [[2016–17 Akron Zips men's basketball team|Akron]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.cleveland.com/sports/college/index.ssf/2017/03/nit_2017_akron_zips.html|title=NIT 2017: Akron Zips hold off Houston, 78–75|work=cleveland.com|access-date=2017-07-24|language=en-US}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
